faq.question: When should I use local browse or a hosted session?
faq.answer: Use local browse to explore an accessible page with your local Chrome. A hosted session is useful when the workflow needs a remotely managed browser; check its account and service requirements separately.

faq.question: Which MCP documentation is current?

faq.question: What is the browse Skill for?
faq.answer: It teaches a coding agent to use the browse CLI. It is a companion entry point for browser tasks, not an additional hosted browser entitlement.

faq.question: Does local use always require a subscription?
faq.answer: The documented local browse mode differs from hosted Browserbase sessions. Check the chosen interface rather than applying cloud billing assumptions to all project use.

faq.question: How should older examples be interpreted?
faq.answer: Treat them as version-specific. Confirm the installed Stagehand major and current API before translating an old example into a maintained workflow.

overview.title: About Chrome DevTools
paragraphs: The ChromeDevTools organization publishes tools around Chrome’s developer diagnostics, including chrome-devtools-mcp. The project connects coding agents to browser inspection and automation rather than supplying a general-purpose language model.

Chrome DevTools provides inspection of a running Chrome page; the MCP project exposes diagnostic tools to an agent. Network requests, performance traces, and runtime state answer different questions. The browser remains the source of measurements, while the agent combines those observations into hypotheses that can be checked.

Its repository includes the server, client setup, official Skills, and troubleshooting. Follow the configuration and enabled capabilities of the installed release; a server tool, a CLI path, and a usage Skill are related interfaces rather than separate publishers.

faq.question: Are the debugging Skills official?

faq.question: Where should launch failures be investigated?
